summary.text: Diatoms are single-celled algae found in oceans, waterways and soils, each surrounded by a cell wall of silica called a frustule.
They are estimated to carry out about half of photosynthesis in the global oceans and to generate 20 to 50 percent of the oxygen produced on the planet each year.
Their shells pile up in marine sediment and in diatomaceous earth, a crumbly rock used for water filtration, mild abrasives and cat litter.

facts.label: Documented species
facts.value: About 12,000, with many more thought undocumented

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: During or before the early Jurassic

items.prompt: Each year winds carry millions of tons of diatom shell dust across the Atlantic to fertilize the Amazon basin. Where does it come from?
items.explain: The dust blows across the Atlantic from the African Sahara, much of it from the Bodélé Depression, once a system of freshwater lakes.

items.prompt: Why would a shortage of silicon in seawater hit diatoms especially hard?

options.label: Their cell walls are built from silica
Silicon is what makes them float
They need it to digest their prey
Their chlorophyll is made from it

items.explain: Diatoms are enclosed in silica walls, and they take in over 6.7 billion tonnes of silicon a year from the waters they live in.

items.prompt: With plenty of sunlight and nutrients, about how long does a population of living diatoms take to double?
items.explain: Given adequate nutrients and sunlight, a diatom assemblage doubles roughly every 24 hours by dividing.

items.prompt: A diatom ends up many kilometres from where it started. What most likely carried it there?

options.label: The beating of its own flagella

items.explain: Diatoms move mostly passively with ocean currents and wind-induced turbulence; most cells lack flagella.

items.prompt: Diatoms are nicknamed "living opals" because of how they shimmer. What produces their colours?

options.label: Glowing chemicals made in the cell
The structure of their silica walls
Oil droplets on the cell surface
Dyes taken in from their food

items.explain: The silica frustules produce structural coloration, which earned diatoms names like "jewels of the sea" and "living opals".

items.prompt: Diatoms drift in the water and make food from light, like plants. Which plankton type are they?
items.explain: Diatoms photosynthesize and are a type of phytoplankton; as eukaryotes they are not bacteria.
